def seeded_dropout {sg : Bool} {w : Nat} (x_ptr output_ptr : Ptr .f32) (n_elements : I32)
    (p : F32) (seed : IntV sg w) (BLOCK_SIZE : Nat) : Kernel where
entries.note: the two pointers are `*fp32` (the host passes `float32` tensors); `n_elements` is an `int32`: an integer argument in `[-2^31, 2^31)` other than `1` is a runtime `int32` (SEMANTICS.md, Scalar arguments; `Inst.ok.n_lt`), and at `n = 1` it is the constant `1`, which line 124 makes an `int32` tensor before comparing, so the model is the same (`model`'s docstring); `p` is a Python `float`, the runtime `float32` `FloatV.hostF32` of the double (`p32`); `seed` is a Python `int`, a runtime `int32`, `int64` or `uint64` by its value (the implicit `sg`, `w`; `model` picks the type), and at `seed = 1` the constant `1`, which `tl.rand` makes an `int32` tensor (`tl.to_tensor`) before any use, so the model is the `int32` one; the constexpr `BLOCK_SIZE` is a Lean parameter; no parameter has a default

the constexpr `BLOCK_SIZE`, an operand of `*` with the `int32` tensor `pid`, is built in `int32`, modulo `2^32` (SEMANTICS.md, Constants); the product is the wrapping `int32` product, which does not wrap on covered instances (`Block.Fits`)
the `int32` scalar `block_start` added to every lane of the `int32` `tl.arange` (the library's scalar-tensor `+`); wrapping, which does not happen on covered instances

`int32` tensor against the `int32` scalar `n_elements`, broadcast to every lane: the signed `int32` comparison; at `n = 1` the constant `1` first becomes an `int32` tensor (SEMANTICS.md, Constants: everywhere else), the same comparison
`x_ptr + offsets` advances the `*fp32` pointer by each lane's `int32` offset, in elements; mask as in the source, no `other` (disabled lanes are unspecified), no performance-only argument

`tl.rand(seed, offsets)` with the default 10 rounds (`TVA.Lang.Random`; SEMANTICS.md, Random numbers): `randint4x` on the `int32` offsets (the counter `(offsets.to(uint32), 0, 0, 0)`, since the offsets are 32 bits wide) and the key from `seed.to(uint64)`, then `uint_to_uniform_float`, an `itof` and an IEEE product with `Philox.scale32`; the helpers are Triton's library functions (`triton.language.random`), whose meaning is the library's; computed on every lane, the disabled ones included

`random > p`: the `float32` block against the runtime `float32` scalar `p` (no promotion, both `float32`), Triton's ordered `>` (`arith.cmpf ogt`), written as the ordered `p < random` (`FloatV.lt`; both false on NaN); the product inside `tl.rand` reaches only this comparison, never an addition, so nothing can fuse with it (SEMANTICS.md, Float `+` and `-`)

`1 - p`: the Python `1`, an operand of `-` with the `float32` scalar `p`, built in `float32` (`one32`, `FloatV.litF32` of the double `1.0`; SEMANTICS.md, Constants), and the IEEE `float32` subtraction `tl.sub` (no product feeds it); `x / (1 - p)`: the block divided by the broadcast scalar, the platform's `float32` division `tl.div` (`div.full.f32`, `Rules.Num.DivFull`), on every lane; `tl.where(x_keep, …, 0.0)`: the `int1` condition `x_keep`, and the Python `0.0`, a value of `tl.where`, built in `float32` as `+0` (`FloatV.litF32 (FloatV.ofPat 0)`)
`output` is already `float32`, the pointer's dtype, so no conversion; mask as in the source
